description: We are a team of engineers based in the Chicagoland area. From Northwestern University and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, we are super excited to share our project with the larger community.
summary: We built Overtone to help blind and low-vision visitors explore NASA’s Earth Information Center through sound. Overtone turns brightness, color, edges, and motion into musical patterns that visitors can hear and compare. Visitors can explore 85 curated artifacts across nine exhibits, from Sea Level’s ambient drones to Wildfires’ industrial percussion. Each exhibit has a distinct musical style, and each image shapes its own score. We added keyboard navigation, touch controls, and screen-reader announcements so visitors can explore the gallery independently.
details:
We use Node.js, Sharp, and FFmpeg to extract features from NASA imagery. In the browser, TypeScript maps those features to music, Web Audio plays the score, and Canvas draws a synchronized playhead. For example, Sea Level follows image motion to guide sustained notes, while Wildfires uses warm colors and visual change to set percussion density. In the Lab, visitors can customize the mappings for all 184 catalog artifacts.

We build with Vite and deploy to Azure Static Web Apps through GitHub Actions. We used test-driven development (TDD), linters, style checkers, and mutation testing to check behavior, keep the code consistent, and verify that my tests catch changes in behavior.

My next step is to test Overtone with blind and low-vision visitors and learn which sounds best help them navigate the gallery and distinguish artifacts.
